question: Does the Q4_K LM-head shared-memory activation cache (candidate.patch, originally 0e0c5276) improve complete-request latency on Apple M3 Chrome/Metal without changing tokens, text, cancellation, session reuse, unload or device recreation?

arms.A: Doppler main at the commit that adds this contract (source identical to 36ce6036); lm_head_argmax_q4k.wgsl is the pre-0e0c5276 kernel
arms.B: Arm A plus candidate.patch (lm_head_argmax_q4k.wgsl and its kernel-ref digest only)

model.directory: .cache/qwen-2b-standard-blake3-20261017 on Mars (the retained Mac contract directory); weight bytes must equal the AMD copy

design.unit: one independent Node process launching one fresh headless Chrome process, opening the model once
design.order: blocks alternate ABBA and BAAB; 10 blocks = 20 processes per arm
design.browser: Google Chrome stable via Playwright channel=chrome, --use-angle=metal
design.contention: gpu_busy_percent is Linux-only; record other GPU clients (Activity Monitor GPU history or powermetrics) before and after the run

primaryMetric: per-process median of the 5 warm complete-request wall times (generate() call start to iterator end)
secondaryMetrics: decode and prefill stats from getStats()
analysis: paired by block position: log(B/A) for adjacent A,B processes within each block (2 pairs per block, 20 pairs). Report mean, median, 95% t-interval and 10000-resample percentile bootstrap interval of the mean log ratio, expressed as percent change.

promotionRule.parity: every request in every process of both arms yields identical token IDs and text; A and B must match each other
promotionRule.lifecycle: every process completes the lifecycle sequence: the cancelled request rejects with AbortError after a proper prefix of the expected tokens, the reuse and device-recreation requests reproduce the expected tokens and text exactly, unload() and destroyDevice() succeed, and Chrome exits cleanly
promotionRule.latency: upper bound of the 95% bootstrap interval of mean warm complete-request percent change (B vs A) is below 0
promotionRule.otherwise: retain the kernel measurement as an operator-level result; make no release or complete-request claim on this platform

crossPlatform: Run on M3 (contract-v3-metal.json, Mars) and AMD (contract-v3.json, Jupiter). A shared default needs both to pass; a single-platform pass can only justify an explicitly selected platform variant.

amends.reason: The owner restated the promotion gate on 2026-10-22 to require exact cancellation, reuse, unload and device recreation in addition to tokens and text; arms move to current main because 0428c15a is no longer the head.

runtimeProfileEffect: Mac product lane: useGreedyLmHeadArgmaxFusion=true, lmHeadArgmaxQ4K {useFullBlockFastPath: true, colsPerWorkgroup: 128, threadsPerCol: 2}, q4k_metal_simd16 fused FFN, decodeLoop batchSize 8
preconditions: a kernel-timing probe in each arm shows decode lm_head_argmax_q4k phase1 dispatches before the latency comparison is run

lifecycleChecks.sequence: after the timed requests, in the same session: abort one request from onToken after its 4th token; run one full request (reuse after cancellation); unload(); destroyDevice(); load() again on a new device and run one full request; unload(); destroyDevice(); close Chrome. Not timed for the primary metric.
lifecycleChecks.abortContract: load() is the compat facade; its generate() rejects with AbortError per src/inference/pipelines/text/abort-contract.js. DOPPLER_GENERATION_ABORTED belongs to Capsule operations, not this surface.
